messages.subject: Spatial model with observations in inlabru
parts:
Hello,
I am new to inlabru and I have some questions for the implementation of the following model:

Y(s) = intercept + \beta*X + u(s)+ \epsilon(s) where \epsilon(s) is Gaussian with variance \sigma²Id. Y(s) and X are vector of size 445 for which I have data. And u(s) is the spatial random effect with a matern covariance.

Following the SVC tutorial in inlabru I implement it that way:
hull <- fm_extensions(
df_FRANCE_count,
convex = c(100, 600),
concave = c(250, 600)
)

spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
mesh = mesh,
prior.range = c(100000, 0.25), # P(range < 100000) = 0.25
prior.sigma = c(1, 0.15) # P(sigma > 1) = 0.15
)

res_spatial <- bru(
components = ~ -1 + intercept(1) + X + u(geometry, model = spde),
like(
formula = Y~.,
family = "gaussian",
data = df
),
options = list(
control.compute = list(waic = TRUE, cpo = FALSE),
control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
verbose = FALSE
)
)

This code is running and I don't have errors but I do have some questions:
1) How does the observed covariables X that are size 445 are taken into account since my mesh is of size 1206 ? I want to be sure that the model will use the covariates X that are observed for the Y(s) that are observed and estimates them for the other points of the mesh.

2) I wanted to implement an RSR method using the extracontstr=
X_i <- cbind(rep(1, length(X)), X)
Q <- qr.Q( qr(X_i) )
e <- rep(0, nrow(constr))
extraconstr=list(A= constr, e=e)
but it's not working and I have an error due to dimensions:
  iinla: Problem in inla: Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  ncol in matrix A(extraconstr) does not correspont to the length of f: 445 1206
Am I not using the option well ?

3) Does the res_spatial$summary.fitted.values are the \hat(Y) ? I saw that we have predictors for the 445 observations and then for all the points of the mesh.
And can I use them to plot a map or the predict() is doing the same ?

4)
pred_spatial <- predict(res_spatial, fm_pixels(mesh), ~ intercept + u + X))
I tried using the predict function but I do have a warning concerning the covariates X:
The input evaluation 'X' for 'X' failed. Perhaps the data object doesn't contain the needed variables? Falling back to '1'.
Maybe I didn't understand how the predict function was working but I didn't found examples with spatial and observations at the same time.

Thank you for your help,
Best Regards
Alizée

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial model with observations in inlabru
parts:
Hi,

the way you defined the components, the X values at the observation
locations need to be provided in the input data. Your model definition
links each X=value to a corresponding observation, without involving
space at all, so it will use the appropriate values and doesn't
involve the mesh. The mesh is only involved when evaluating the
u-component.

In your predict() call, you've only provided locations, but no X
values. Add the X-values for the fm_pixels() locations to the newdata
input and it should work; you need newdata to have the same
information about model inputs as your original estimation data
(except the response variable which isn't needed/used).

If you want X to be evaluated automatically (e.g. from a raster) based
on the locations/geometry, you need to redefine the X-component to
take the raster as input, so inlabru can evaluate it at the given
prediction locations.
(alternatively, use X_eval(eval_spatial(the_raster, .data.)) instead
of X in the prediction expression).

Personally, I would just use predict() for all posterior quantities
beyond the very basic fit$summary.fixed and fit$summary.random output.
I find keeping track of what elements are where in fitted.values is
rarely worth the hassle. That being said, it first N values of it will
match the observation ordering.

Finn

parts:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your answer to my previous questions.

I have real datas and really wish to obtains maps from them and the predictions from INLA.
Can I use the fitted.Predictor given by bru to obtain a maps as follow ? 
# get easting and northing limits
bbox <- fm_bbox(hull[[1]])
grd_dims <- round(c(x = diff(bbox[[1]]), y = diff(bbox[[2]])) / 2000)

# make mesh projector to get model summaries from the mesh to the mapping grid
mesh_proj <- fm_evaluator(
new_mesh,
xlim = c(100000, 1400000), ylim = c(5900000, 7150000), dims = grd_dims
)

# make a terra raster stack with the posterior median and range95
make_terra_raster_stack <- function(pred_grids) {
out_stk <- rast()


for (j in 1:1) {
mean_j <- cbind(expand.grid(x = mesh_proj$x, y = mesh_proj$y),
Z = c(matrix(pred_grids[[j]][, 1], grd_dims[1]))
)
mean_j <- rast(mean_j, crs = "EPSG:2154")
range95_j <- cbind(expand.grid(X = mesh_proj$x, Y = mesh_proj$y),
Z = c(matrix(pred_grids[[j]][, 2], grd_dims[1]))
)
range95_j <- rast(range95_j, crs = "EPSG:2154")
out_j <- c(mean_j, range95_j)
terra::add(out_stk) <- out_j
}
names(out_stk) <- c(
"u_median", "u_range95"
)
out_stk <- terra::crop(out_stk, states, mask = TRUE)
return(out_stk)
}


make_plot_field <- function(data_stk, scale_label, title) {
ggplot(states) +
geom_sf(fill = NA) +
coord_sf(datum = NA) +
geom_spatraster(data = data_stk) +
labs(x = "", y = "") +
scale_fill_distiller(scale_label,
palette = "Spectral",
na.value = "transparent"
) +
theme_bw() +
ggtitle(title) +
geom_sf(fill = NA)
}

pred <- data.frame(
median = exp(res_svc_plus$summary.fitted.values[446:4017,"0.5quant"]),
range95 = exp(res_svc_plus$summary.fitted.values[446:4017,"0.975quant"]) -
exp(res_svc_plus$summary.fitted.values[446:4017,"0.025quant"])
)

pred_grids <- lapply(
list(pred = pred),
function(x) as.matrix(fm_evaluate(mesh_proj, x))
)

out_stk <- make_terra_raster_stack(pred_grids = pred_grids)
plot_pred_median <- make_plot_field(
data_stk = out_stk[["u_median"]],
scale_label = "posterior\nmedian\nCd_mousse_s",
title
)

Best regards,
Alizée

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial model with observations in inlabru
parts:
This relies on the details of how you’ve specified the input data and predictor expression in the model estimation; if possible, don’t rely on the hardcoded indexing into fitted.values (it looks like it assumes the specific fitted.values correspond to the field values at the mesh nodes perhaps?), but rather extract the relevant rows by name or similar (or saved information based on how you specified your input data). Otherwise it looks plausible, if you’re extracting the correct information from fitted.values (which may or may not be true, depending on how you setup the model). 
Like I said in my previous reply, I would do this with predict() instead.
Finn

Le vendredi 26 avril 2024 à 17:53:02 UTC+2, Finn Lindgren a écrit :
Hi,

the way you defined the components, the X values at the observation
locations need to be provided in the input data. Your model definition
links each X=value to a corresponding observation, without involving
space at all, so it will use the appropriate values and doesn't
involve the mesh. The mesh is only involved when evaluating the
u-component.

In your predict() call, you've only provided locations, but no X
values. Add the X-values for the fm_pixels() locations to the newdata
input and it should work; you need newdata to have the same
information about model inputs as your original estimation data
(except the response variable which isn't needed/used).

If you want X to be evaluated automatically (e.g. from a raster) based
on the locations/geometry, you need to redefine the X-component to
take the raster as input, so inlabru can evaluate it at the given
prediction locations.
(alternatively, use X_eval(eval_spatial(the_raster, .data.)) instead
of X in the prediction expression).

Personally, I would just use predict() for all posterior quantities
beyond the very basic fit$summary.fixed and fit$summary.random output.
I find keeping track of what elements are where in fitted.values is
rarely worth the hassle. That being said, it first N values of it will
match the observation ordering.

Finn
